summary: Design a manager for seats 1..n that reserves the smallest-numbered free seat and can unreserve any reserved seat.
mainInsight: reserve needs the minimum of a set that changes with inserts (unreserve) and removals (reserve): a min-heap of free seats gives O(log n) for both. A pointer to the next never-used seat avoids heapifying all n seats up front.
invariant: The heap plus the seats >= next form exactly the set of free seats.
canonicalApproach: Min-heap of unreserved seats + next-seat pointer

approaches.name: Boolean array, scan for the first free seat
Min-heap of all free seats
approaches.timeComplexity: O(n) init, O(log n) per op

approaches.name: Min-heap of unreserved seats + next-seat pointer
approaches.summary: Heap only holds returned seats; otherwise hand out next and increment it.
approaches.timeComplexity: O(1) init, O(log n) per op

approaches.name: Sorted set
approaches.summary: SortedList of free seats; pop the first, add on unreserve.

personalSolution.approach: Min-heap of all free seats built with heapify
personalSolution.timeComplexity: O(n) init, O(log n) per reserve/unreserve
personalSolution.notes: Optimal per operation. The next-seat pointer variant avoids building the n-element heap and keeps the heap small, which is worth mentioning.

commonMistakes: Scanning an array for the first free seat on every reserve (O(n) per call).
Using a plain list and min() / remove() (O(n) per call).
With the pointer variant, forgetting that a freed seat is always below next, so the heap must be checked first.
edgeCases: Unreserve the seat just reserved, then reserve again.
Unreserve several seats in decreasing order.

cards.answer: Min-heap of available seats. Clue: reserve must return the smallest-numbered unreserved seat while unreserve keeps adding seats back, with up to 10^5 calls in total.

cards.explanation: Repeated 'give me the minimum' on a set with inserts and deletes is the job of a min-heap.

alsoValid.name: Boolean array scanned for the first free seat on each reserve

promptVariants: In the pointer variant, why is it safe to check the heap before next?
Why is any seat in the freed heap smaller than next?
options: Only seats below next were ever handed out
The heap always holds the n smallest seats
unreserve rejects seats bigger than next
next is reset to 1 whenever the heap is empty
cards.answer: Only seats below next were ever handed out
cards.explanation: A seat can only be unreserved after being reserved, and reserved seats are all < next, so a non-empty heap always holds the smallest free seat.

incorrectOptionExplanations.The heap always holds the n smallest sea: The heap only holds returned seats; it may be empty or small.
incorrectOptionExplanations.unreserve rejects seats bigger than next: No check is needed; the guarantee comes from the reservation order.

promptVariants: Why not keep a boolean array and scan for the first free seat?
What is wrong with an O(n) scan per reserve here?
options: Up to 10^5 calls on 10^5 seats is about 10^10 steps
Boolean arrays cannot represent seat numbers
Scanning returns the largest seat, not the smallest
It cannot support unreserve at all
cards.answer: Up to 10^5 calls on 10^5 seats is about 10^10 steps
cards.explanation: Each reserve can scan O(n), so worst case O(n * calls); the heap makes each operation O(log n).

incorrectOptionExplanations.Boolean arrays cannot represent seat num: The index is the seat number; representation is fine.
incorrectOptionExplanations.Scanning returns the largest seat, not t: A left-to-right scan returns the smallest; speed is the problem.
incorrectOptionExplanations.It cannot support unreserve at all: Unreserve is a simple flag reset.

promptVariants: SeatManager(4); reserve, reserve, reserve, unreserve(3), unreserve(1), reserve. What does the last reserve return?
After reserving 1, 2, 3 and unreserving 3 then 1, what does reserve() return?
cards.explanation: The free seats are {1, 3, 4}. The smallest is 1, regardless of unreserve order.

incorrectOptionExplanations.3: That is the first seat unreserved, but reserve wants the smallest.
incorrectOptionExplanations.4: That is the next never-used seat; returned seats 1 and 3 are smaller.

promptVariants: What are the costs of reserve and unreserve in the canonical code?

cards.explanation: heappop and heappush on a heap of at most n entries are O(log n); handing out next is O(1).

incorrectOptionExplanations.O(log n) reserve, O(n) unreserve: Pushing onto a heap is O(log n).
